spec.doc: Records `signer`'s vote for `outcome` (allowed only once `close_time` has passed). `Invalid` claims the question is unanswerable; an `Invalid` proposal finalizes by voiding the market. Split votes: every outcome, `Invalid` included, has its own counter, and a signer is deduplicated per `(outcome, signer)`, so one signer may attest several outcomes (existing behaviour, extended to `Invalid`). The first outcome to reach threshold becomes the proposal and later `Yes`/`No` quorums never move it. The one exception: `Invalid` reaching threshold replaces a pending `Yes`/`No` proposal and restarts the dispute window, because a quorum saying the question cannot be answered outranks an answer to it. An `Invalid` proposal is never replaced. (Requiring `Invalid` to beat every other count is a possible follow-up.)
spec.name: attest

spec.doc: Attests to an outcome backed by an on-chain reasoning trace in reasoning-registry.
spec.name: attest_with_evidence

spec.doc: Total proposal cancellations executed by the guardian for `market_id`.
spec.name: cancel_count

spec.doc: Guardian action: withdraws an unfinalized signer proposal during the dispute window subject to a rate limit of MAX_CANCELS_PER_MARKET. Works the same for an `Invalid` proposal. Only the proposal is removed: attestations and per-outcome counts stay, so the next attestation that brings any outcome to threshold (for example a further `Yes` once `Yes` already has quorum) proposes again.
spec.name: cancel_proposal

spec.doc: Cancels a pending rotation for a committee (admin only).
spec.name: cancel_rotation

spec.doc: Pays a settled dispute's bond to its payee (the disputer, or the market-core treasury when the proposal was upheld). Permissionless.
spec.name: claim_dispute_bond

spec.doc: Creates a reusable committee with an admin, member set, threshold, and time-lock delay.
spec.name: create_committee

spec.doc: Current attestation round of a weighted-key market; the `round` argument of `submit_signatures` and part of every signed message.
spec.name: current_round

spec.doc: Challenges the current proposal of a `SignersDisputable` market while its dispute window is still open (strictly before `proposed_at + dispute_window`, the instant `finalize_signers` becomes callable). The disputer escrows `dispute_bond` of the collateral token, which freezes finalization until the escalation authority rules or `escalation_timeout` lapses. `alternative` is the outcome the disputer claims is correct (`None`: the market is invalid); it only informs the ruling and must differ from the proposal (so `None` is rejected for an `Invalid` proposal). The disputer may also be a proposing signer.
spec.name: dispute

spec.doc: Committee escalation: each member votes once; the first verdict to gather `k` votes settles the dispute.
spec.name: escalation_attest

spec.doc: Reads the evidence citation at `index` for `market_id`.
spec.name: evidence_at

spec.doc: Reads the currently configured evidence settings, if any.
spec.name: evidence_config

spec.doc: Total evidence citations recorded for `market_id`.
spec.name: evidence_count

spec.doc: Permissionlessly executes a matured rotation for a committee, bumping its epoch.
spec.name: execute_rotation

spec.doc: Permissionless fallback when the escalation authority never rules: `escalation_timeout` after the dispute opened, the bond is refunded and the market is voided, so neither side wins by default.
spec.name: expire_dispute

spec.doc: Permissionless liveness fallback: once `resolution_deadline` has passed, anyone may void a market that is still unresolved, so collateral is never locked behind a missing reveal, a dead feed or silent signers. Resolution is preferred over voiding. A price market whose feed is valid right now is *resolved* instead (so a stalled caller can never force a void on a resolvable market), and a market with a pending signer proposal is refused with `ResolutionAvailable` until `finalize_signers` settles it.
spec.name: expire_market

spec.doc: Settles the pending proposal once its dispute window has elapsed: `Yes`/`No` resolve the market, `Invalid` voids it (and emits `CommitteeVoided`). market-core's `void_market` has no `close_time` guard, but every attestation path requires `now >= close_time` before any write, so no proposal (and no void) can exist before close.
spec.name: finalize_signers

spec.doc: Reads committee state and extends its storage TTL.
spec.name: get_committee

spec.doc: Returns the guardian reason codes valid for `market_id` right now.
spec.name: guardian_options

spec.doc: Guardian action: voids a market subject to verified on-chain reason codes and grace periods.
spec.name: guardian_void_market

spec.doc: Opens fallback signer attestation in a hybrid market if the feed failed past the deadline.
spec.name: open_fallback

spec.doc: The pending admin proposal, including its expiry, if one exists.
spec.name: pending_admin

spec.doc: Starts a two-step handover of the admin role. The new admin must call `accept_admin` itself, so a typo cannot hand control to an address nobody holds.
spec.name: propose_admin

spec.doc: Proposes a new member set and threshold for a committee, executable after rotation_delay.
spec.name: propose_rotation

spec.doc: Registers a reusable committee specification for `market_id`.
spec.name: register_committee_spec

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, signer mode whose proposals can be challenged with a bond (see `dispute`).
spec.name: register_disputable_spec

spec.doc: Registers a hybrid resolution specification (price feed with attested fallback).
spec.name: register_hybrid_spec

spec.doc: Reveals the resolution rule committed to at market creation. Anyone may call this (there is no admin gate) because the only thing that makes a spec acceptable is that it hashes to `market.resolution_hash` — the commitment, not the caller, is the authority. Fails if a spec was already registered for this market.
spec.name: register_price_spec

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, signer mode.
spec.name: register_signer_spec

spec.doc: Reveals a rule committed to through a [`ResolutionSpecV2`] envelope. The envelope must name this network and this resolver's market-core (`DomainMismatch`), use a non-zero salt and the current `version` (`InvalidConfig`), and hash to the market's commitment (`SpecHashMismatch`). The inner rule is then validated and stored exactly as the legacy entrypoints do.
spec.name: register_spec_v2

spec.doc: See `register_price_spec` — same commit/reveal rule, weighted Ed25519 committee that signs off-chain and is verified by `submit_signatures`.
spec.name: register_weighted_key_spec

spec.doc: When `expire_market` becomes callable for `market_id`: `close_time` plus [`RESOLUTION_GRACE_SECS`]. Needs only market-core's `close_time`, so it is known before (and without) a spec reveal.
spec.name: resolution_deadline

spec.doc: Configures the reasoning registry contract address and evidence policy (admin only).
spec.name: set_evidence_config

spec.doc: Guardian escalation: the admin rules on an open dispute.
spec.name: settle_dispute

spec.doc: The price pinned by `snapshot_price`, if any.
spec.name: snapshot

spec.doc: Pins the committed feed's price for `close_time` in resolver storage, so `resolve_price` still works after the oracle's bounded history has aged that record out (SEP-40 `price(asset, timestamp)` returns `None` outside the retained window). Permissionless: `caller` only authorizes being recorded as `taken_by`. Callable any time after `close_time` while the market is unresolved, but in practice it must run within the oracle's retention window (see `docs/architecture.md`, "Oracle history retention"). The first valid snapshot wins (`SnapshotExists` afterwards): for a fixed `(asset, close_time)` the answer is deterministic, and freezing it deliberately prefers determinism over an oracle later rewriting history. A price `resolve_price` would reject is never stored.
spec.name: snapshot_price

spec.doc: Counts Ed25519 signatures from a weighted committee. Permissionless: the signatures, not the submitter, carry the authority. Each signature is over the message built by `attestation_message`; non-members and keys that already signed this round (for either outcome) are skipped, and a single invalid signature aborts the whole batch, so submitters should pre-filter with a verifier. Once the accumulated weight for `outcome` first reaches the threshold a proposal is recorded and the dispute window starts; later calls never move it.
spec.name: submit_signatures

spec.doc: Stored link connecting an attestation to a reasoning registry trace. `outcome` was a market-core `Outcome` before `Invalid` attestations; the two enums encode `Yes`/`No` identically, so earlier entries still decode.
spec.name: AttestationEvidence

void_v0.doc: The question is ambiguous or unanswerable; finalizing voids the market.
void_v0.name: Invalid

spec.doc: What a signer attests to. Resolver-local so market-core's `Outcome` (and the vendored `market_core.wasm`) never gains an `Invalid` variant: an `Invalid` proposal finalizes through market-core's `void_market` instead of `resolve`. Never part of a `ResolutionSpec`, so commitment hashes are unaffected (ADR 0001).
spec.name: AttestedOutcome

spec.doc: Reusable committee managed by an admin under time-locked rotation rules.
spec.name: Committee

spec.doc: Binds a market to a reusable committee registry subject to rotation bounds.
spec.name: CommitteeRef

spec.doc: Attested resolution whose proposal can be challenged with a bond during the dispute window. Hashed as `ResolutionSpec::SignersDisputable`, a separate variant, so existing `Signers` commitments are unaffected.

fields.doc: Collateral escrowed by `dispute`; must be positive.
fields.name: dispute_bond

fields.doc: Seconds after a dispute opens before anyone may void it unresolved.
fields.name: escalation_timeout

spec.name: DisputableSignerConfig

tuple_v0.doc: `k` of these members, through `escalation_attest`. Must be disjoint from the proposing signers.
tuple_v0.name: Committee

spec.doc: Who rules on a dispute.
spec.name: Escalation

spec.doc: Evidence policy governing whether attestation evidence is required.
spec.name: EvidencePolicy

spec.doc: Which resolution path a market was on when it expired.
spec.name: ExpiryMode

spec.doc: Guardian action type emitted for audit trails.
spec.name: GuardianActionKind

void_v0.doc: Proposal exists and dispute window is currently active.
void_v0.name: DisputeUpheld

void_v0.doc: Price mode, past close_time + ORACLE_GRACE_SECS, price feed unavailable or stale.
void_v0.name: OracleUnavailable

void_v0.doc: Signer mode, past close_time + SIGNER_GRACE_SECS, no proposal.
void_v0.name: SignersStalled

void_v0.doc: Past close_time + REVEAL_GRACE_SECS, no spec revealed.
void_v0.name: UnrevealedSpec

spec.doc: Reason code constraining guardian interventions.
spec.name: GuardianReason

spec.doc: Dual-path resolution mode: price feed first, falling back to signers.
spec.name: HybridConfig

spec.doc: A proposed admin handover (#62). Absent when no transfer is pending.
spec.name: PendingAdmin

spec.doc: A price read pinned by [`Resolver::snapshot_price`] so resolution survives the oracle aging the `close_time` record out of its history.
spec.name: PriceSnapshot

spec.doc: The full resolution rule a market's `resolution_hash` commits to. Hashing this (rather than the bare `PriceConfig`/`SignerConfig`) keeps the two modes in disjoint hash spaces even if their field encodings could otherwise collide. See `docs/adr/0001-resolution-commitment.md`.
spec.name: ResolutionSpec

spec.doc: Versioned commitment envelope. Unlike a bare [`ResolutionSpec`] it binds the network and the market-core instance, and carries a creator-chosen `salt` that makes a pre-reveal brute-force of the (low-entropy) rule infeasible.
spec.name: ResolutionSpecV2

void_v0.doc: A bonded dispute is open; finalization is frozen until it settles.
void_v0.name: Disputed

void_v0.doc: Voided by [`Resolver::expire_market`] after the resolution deadline.
void_v0.name: Expired

spec.doc: The escalation authority's ruling. `Invalid` voids the market.
spec.name: Verdict

fields.doc: Raw Ed25519 public key. For a `G...` account address this is `StrKey.decodeEd25519PublicKey(address)`; `C...` addresses have none.
fields.name: pubkey

fields.doc: Total weight that must sign one outcome. Choose it above half the total weight so two outcomes can never both reach it.
fields.name: weight_threshold

cases.doc: A proposed admin handover was not accepted within its `expires_at`.
cases.name: PendingAdminExpired

spec.doc: A signer committee finalized an `Invalid` proposal and voided the market. Distinguishes committee voids from `GuardianAction { action: Void }`.
spec.name: CommitteeVoided

spec.doc: `disputer_won` is true when the bond returns to the disputer because the ruling overturned the proposal. A timeout (`expire_dispute`) also refunds the bond but is reported as `verdict: Invalid, disputer_won: false`. That pair also describes a ruling of `Invalid` that upholds an `Invalid` proposal; the two differ in the bond's payee (disputer on timeout, market-core treasury when upheld), readable from the `Dispute` entry until `claim_dispute_bond` runs. `payout` is the escrowed bond, claimable by its payee.
spec.name: DisputeSettled

params.doc: What the disputer claims is correct; `None` claims the market is invalid.
params.name: alternative

spec.doc: `proposal_outcome` (like `Attested::outcome`) was a market-core `Outcome`; `Yes`/`No` encode identically, so only `Invalid` is new to decoders.
spec.name: FallbackSuperseded

spec.doc: `PriceResolution` plus whether the price came from a stored [`PriceSnapshot`]. Both are emitted for one release so indexers decoding `PriceResolution` keep working while they move to this event.
spec.name: PriceResolutionV2
